Except for uses and disclosures of VA information authorized by this contract for performance of the contract, the contractor may use and disclose VA information only in two situations: (i) in response to a qualifying order of a court of competent jurisdiction after notification to VA CO (ii) with written approval from the VA CO. The contractor shall refer all requests for, demands for production of or inquiries about, VA information and information systems to the VA CO for response. k. Notwithstanding the provision above, the contractor shall not release VA records protected by Title 38 U.S.C. § 5705, Confidentiality of medical quality assurance records and/or Title 38 U.S.C. § 7332, Confidentiality of certain medical records pertaining to drug addiction, sickle cell anemia, alcoholism or alcohol abuse or infection with Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV). If the contractor is in receipt of a court order or other requests for the abovementioned information, the contractor shall immediately refer such court order or other requests to the VA CO for response. l. Given the rapid obsolescence of COTS components and a high demand for software modernization (cybersecurity patching), the program office requires an optimized sustainment strategy that balances system availability with TOC. 2.1 IBDSS Enterprise Programs: The IBDSS enterprise includes the following programs that must be incorporated into the PS-BCA. 2.1.1 Fixed Site Electronic Security System (ESS) Fixed Site ESS is in the Operations and Support phase. ase Defense Operations Center (BDOC) across 80+ U.S. Air Force installations. The system operates within segmented network environments supporting mission-critical operations, requiring high-availability architecture, controlled software release management, and integration of multiple security technologies into a unified operational platform. 2.1.4 Deployable-Mobile Security Awareness Tool (DMSAT) DMSAT is currently in the Operations and Support phase. Given the rapid obsolescence of COTS components and a high demand for software modernization (cybersecurity patching), the program office requires an optimized sustainment strategy that balances system availability with TOC. 2.1 IBDSS Enterprise Programs: The IBDSS enterprise includes the following programs that must be incorporated into the PS-BCA. 2.1.1 Fixed Site Electronic Security System (ESS) Fixed Site ESS is in the Operations and Support phase. ESS sustainment currently includes 80+ CONUS and USAFE locations, with modernization upgrades scheduled approximately every ten years. Additional design and install projects are accomplished for AF National Guard and Reserve sites; however, sustainment of those locations is not

tailored components. Except for nuclear and presidential systems, the within-scope ESS is currently sustained by contract logistics support. 2.1.2 Remote Target Engagement System (RTES) RTES is in the Operations and Support phase. This system includes remotely operated weapons, fielded at a handful of nuclear security sites. It is fixed site system that includes integrated developmental, COTS and commercial tailored components. PL-1N systems, including RTES and Fixed Site ESS, are sustained organically by Visual Imagery and Intrusion Detection Systems (VIIDS) maintainers at the organizational level and by the Cryptologic and Cyber Systems Division (CCSD) sustainment depot at Lackland AFB, TX. 2.1.3 Physical Security Information Management (PSIM) PSIM is currently in the Operations and Support phase. Platform for Integrated Command, Control and Communications, and Responsive Defense (PICARD) Pivot PSIM is an enterprise physical security software solution designed to modernize the Base Defense Operations Center (BDOC) across 80+ U.S. Air Force installations. The system integrates multiple, unconnected physical security subsystems, including enterprise video management systems, access control systems, intrusion detection systems, GIS-based facility mapping, 3-

sla_onsite.text: onID="2.0.2">CRITERION.EXCLUSION.CONVICTIONS.PARTICIPATION_IN_CRIMINAL_ORGANISATION</cbc:CriterionTypeCode> <cbc:Name>Osalemine kuritegelikus organisatsioonis</cbc:Name> <cbc:Description languageID="ET">Kas ettevõtja ise või tema haldus-, juht- või järelevalveorgani liige või isik, kellel on volitused seda ettevõtjat esindada, tema nimel otsuseid teha või teda kontrollida, on lõpliku süüdimõistva kohtuotsusega süüdi mõistetud kuritegelikus organisatsioonis osalemise eest kõige rohkem viimase viie aasta jooksul või kehtib süüdimõistvas kohtuotsuses sätestatud kõrvalejäämise kohustus endiselt?</cbc:Description> <cac:Legislation> <cbc:ID schemeID="CriteriaTaxonomy" schemeAgencyID="EU-COM-GROW" schemeVersionID="2.0.2">c753a2c5-59e6-4970-b6eb-27224e96bf76</cbc:ID> <cbc:Title languageID="ET">RHS § 95 lg 1 p 1 "keda või kelle haldus-, juhtimis- või järelevalveorgani liiget, prokuristi või muud isikut, kellel on volitus seda ettevõtjat esindada, tema nimel otsuseid teha või teda kontrollida, on karistatud kuritegelikus ühenduses osalemise eest". Kui hankemenetlusest kõrvaldamise alus esineb, võib ettevõtja soovi korral esitada tõendeid selle kohta, et ta on võtnud meetmeid oma usaldusväärsuse taastamiseks. Heastamise võimalus on ettevõtjal juh

Nature of the action being approved (Contractor name, contract type, and total estimated value with options). (a) Nature of action: FEMA intends to procure, on a sole source basis, a one-year continuation bridge Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) for cloud reseller (brokerage) services. This bridge BPA will support the ongoing migration and management of existing systems and data in a cloud environment, with the goal of enhancing cybersecurity, service scalability, service flexibility, data integration, and cost efficiency. OCIO has previously migrated systems and data to Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Microsoft Azure, representing a significant government investment. Therefore, it is essential that this bridge BPA for cloud reseller services includes both AWS and Azure as minimum requirements. While the BPA may also include additional cloud service providers, AWS and Azure must be available as options to ensure continuity of operations during the bridge period. 1 In this document, citations to RFO Part 6, RFO Part 8, RFO Part 25, and HSAR Part 3006 are citatio

vices. The current performance period ends on 03/29/2026, and there is not enough time to conduct a full and open competitive solicitation before this date. While FEMA had planned to transition to a DHS Cloud vehicle, it has been determined that the DHS Cloud vehicle will not be awarded in time to meet our operational needs. The bridge BPA will provide uninterrupted access to Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Microsoft Azure, which are essential for maintaining the agency’s cloud infrastructure and supporting ongoing operations. Any lapse or delay in service would risk significant operational impacts, including potential interruptions to cybersecurity protections, data integration, and service scalability. Therefore, this bridge BPA is essential to maintain continuity of services while FEMA completes the competitive acquisition process for a long-term solution. This approach is in the best interest of the government and supports FEMA’s mission by ensuring the reliability and stability of its cloud environment during the transition period. 5. Contract work shall be acco mplished in a sequential manner, with the realignment work limited to no more than three (3) row s of headstones at any given time in order to minimize overall disruption to the cemetery. Work cannot begin in subsequent burial rows until such time that work has been completed in prior burial rows. Submit proposed project work schedule sequence for COR review and approval prior to start of project. (See B.3 General Conditions, N. SUBMITTALS, “Work plan/Staffing plan”.) 2. Grading and turf renovation work shall typically occur either in conjunction with or prior to specified headstone raise and realign work in order to achieve the specified requirements for flowing precision uniformity of headstones with the leveled burial section surface terrain. 3. Cleaning of the headstones shall begin after all other work has been accepted and completed. F. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE: The Period of Performance is 365 calendar days from Notice to Proceed (NTP), to include the turf establishment period. Turf renovation will only be allowed when the existing turfgrass is actively growing and not in dormancy.

BACKGROUND: The Naval Surface Warfare Center, Carderock Division (NSWCCD) is investigating persistent corrosion preventative compounds (CPCs) for future use in preventing corrosion on ground vehicles and tactical assets operating in a marine environment. A CPC is a material or substance that is applied to a metal surface and creates a barrier that prevents the progression of rust or oxidation on the surface. A persistent CPC will protect the surface from corrosion for a period of no less than 2 years when exposed to an ISO 12944 - C5 (very harsh) environment before reapplication of the substance is required. 1.2. OBJECTIVE: The purpose of this RFI is to conduct market research to identify potential vendors with products available that meet the capability criteria listed in this document. 1.3. DISCLAIMER: This is a Request for Information (RFI) only. This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes and does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. This RFI does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. Responders are advised that the U.S. Government will not

on and planning purposes and does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. This RFI does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. Responders are advised that the U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI. 1.4. REQUIRED CAPABILITY: Product types of interest include, but are not limited to, greases, lubricants, oils, and waxes. The product is required to meet the following criteria: • The applied material provides continuous corrosion prevention for no less than 2 years when exposed to an ISO 12944 – C5 (Very harsh) environment. o No additional touch-up or reapplication during that period. • The product is shelf-stable (Storage temperature range 20 – 120 oF, no greater than 85%RH) for a minimum of 2 years. • Once applied, the product has a consistency and texture that will not accumulate dirt or debris. • The product can be applied and is stable in environments where ambient conditions include temperatures of 75-110ºF and over 90% humidity. • The material is a non-permanent coating. 1.5.
